subtopic: KV cache fragmentation / Paged vs contiguous allocator
learningObjective: Diagnose external fragmentation in a contiguous per-sequence KV allocator vs paged allocation.
stem: A serving stack allocates KV cache as contiguous per-sequence slabs sized to each request's max_new_tokens. Diagnose the memory behavior described below.
profileData:
Setup: 40 GB total KV cache budget.
  Requests come and go with varying max_new_tokens = 512 to 8192.
  Steady-state observation:
    Sum of active sequences' allocated KV: 38 GB
    Sum of KV actually used by generated tokens: 12 GB
    Free KV memory: 2 GB
    New request (max_new_tokens=2048, requires 300 MB contiguous KV): FAILS to allocate despite 2 GB free.
    OOM error reported.

options.text: This is a bug in the KV cache accounting; free memory shows 2 GB but the allocator sees 0. Fix the accounting by including reserved slabs in the free counter, and the new request will succeed.
This is compute-bound behavior: the OOM is a symptom of decode being too slow to release KV blocks quickly enough. Increasing tensor parallelism will speed up decode and prevent OOM.
This is a data race between the scheduler and the allocator; the fix is to serialize KV cache allocation with a global mutex, which will resolve the OOM at the cost of some throughput.

This is textbook external fragmentation from contiguous per-sequence slab allocation: each slab is reserved up-front at max_new_tokens size, so 26 GB of allocated KV is actually unused (reserved for tokens not yet generated), and the 2 GB free area is scattered in non-contiguous pieces too small to fit any single slab. Paged KV cache (fixed-size blocks + indirection) directly addresses this.

explanation: The signature is classic external fragmentation: allocated ≠ used, and the small remaining free memory is not contiguous enough to hold a new slab. The reserved-up-to-max_new_tokens policy causes internal waste (26 GB reserved but not yet used), and freed slabs of varying sizes create external fragmentation. PagedAttention's fixed-size block allocation with block-table indirection eliminates external fragmentation and only over-allocates by at most one block per sequence.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: not an accounting bug; the memory really is fragmented/reserved.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: OOM is a memory-management issue, unrelated to TP or decode speed.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: no data race; the problem is fragmentation.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: external + internal fragmentation from contiguous slab allocation.

assumptions: 'External fragmentation' is used in the OS memory-management sense: free space exists but not in a single contiguous block.
nonImplications: Does not imply paged KV cache has zero waste; it does have small per-sequence internal waste bounded by block size.
Does not imply that all fragmentation problems are solved by paging alone; preemption policy still matters.

performanceClaim.scope: External + internal KV fragmentation from contiguous slab allocation
